claims.text: Plane provides four pricing editions that range from zero to 499 dollars, built for different usage levels and team sizes.

A review states Plane uses a freemium per-seat model with a free tier for up to twelve users, a Pro tier at six dollars per seat per month, a Business tier at thirteen dollars per seat per month, and custom-priced Enterprise Grid plans.
claims.evidence: Plane follows a freemium, per-seat model: the Free tier supports up to 12 users, Pro is $6/seat/month, and Business is $13/seat/month, each with an increasing allocation of AI credits per seat.

claims.text: Plane advertises a free tier with core features alongside paid plans that unlock advanced features, enterprise needs, and priority support.
claims.evidence: Yes, Plane offers a generous free tier with core features. We also have paid plans for advanced features, enterprise needs, and priority support.

claims.text: G2 identifies ClickUp, monday AI Work Platform, and Jira as top alternatives to Plane.
The Plane blog contrasts its platform with ClickUp by describing Plane as a tighter, self-hostable workspace for engineering-led teams versus ClickUp’s broader all-in-one cloud approach.
claims.evidence: Plane took a tighter approach: connect work items, documentation, sprints, intake, and AI in a single workspace that engineering-led teams can self-host, extend, and audit.

claims.text: The Plane blog notes that Plane embeds cycles, epics, and releases in one model, offers native agent features without requiring an additional artificial intelligence purchase, and supports self-hosted deployments, unlike ClickUp.
claims.evidence: Plane runs every team in one workspace, with cycles, epics, and releases built into one model.

claims.text: A customer case study on the Plane website describes how MinimalArt migrated from ClickUp to Plane to automate monthly reporting and gain real-time visibility into workloads.
claims.evidence: Monthly client reporting, once a manual and hours-long process, is now automated through a combination of Plane’s exports, APIs, and a third-party reporting tool.

claims.text: Heise Online reports that Plane is open-source project management software aimed at software developers and positioned as an alternative to Jira, Linear, Monday, and ClickUp.
claims.evidence: Plane is open-source project management software aimed at software developers as an alternative to Jira, Linear, Monday, and ClickUp.

claims.text: An analysis of ClickUp alternatives characterizes Plane as free and self-hostable with a modern interface covering issues, cycles, modules, and roadmaps, but cautions that its documentation and goals features are lighter than ClickUp’s and its ecosystem is newer.
claims.evidence: Docs and goals features are lighter than ClickUp's

claims.text: The Plane blog claims full feature parity with Jira Standard and eighty percent parity with Jira Professional, along with more than fifty thousand self-hosting teams, over one hundred thousand Docker deploys, and forty-four thousand Kubernetes deploys.
claims.evidence: It claims full parity with Jira Standard and 80% parity with Jira Professional, and unlike most tools on this list, it ships AI, documentation, intake, and time tracking as native capabilities rather than plugin afterthoughts.

claims.text: The Plane blog also says Plane includes artificial intelligence, documentation, intake, and time tracking as native built-in features rather than afterthought plugins.

claims.text: A review of open-source project management tools calls Plane the nearest open-source equivalent to Linear and Jira Software, citing fifty-nine thousand one hundred sixteen GitHub stars and near-weekly releases.
claims.evidence: Plane is the closest open source answer to Linear and Jira Software, and it has the most GitHub stars of the six, 59,116.
